entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Lucius Epidius Titius Aquilinus was a Roman senator of the second century, born into a distinguished family of senatorial rank and marrying a noblewoman of the Julia clan. His father, Titius Aquilinus, was consul in 151 CE, and his grandfather, Titus Annius Agrippinus, held the consulship in 125 CE. As a senator, Lucius Titius Epidius Aquilinus played a significant role in the Roman Senate, serving as a magistrate and participating in the governance of the empire. He was known for his wise and just leadership, earning him the respect and admiration of his peers. Despite his important position, little is known about his personal life, and his legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his more famous ancestors. Lucius Titius Epidius Aquilinus died in 200 CE, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated public servant and a testament to the enduring power of Roman tradition. The inscription on his tomb, now lost to history, remains a poignant reminder of his enduring impact on the empire he served.
